key_insight: E-RLBM independently relaxes nonhydrodynamic modes, continuously connecting BGK and regularized collisions while preserving Navier–Stokes viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The two-rate operator offers a low-cost way to improve flow-simulation stability without implementing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.
method: Separate second-order hydrodynamic and complementary kinetic modes.
Assign the kinetic subspace its own relaxation time.
Analyze viscosity and direction-dependent fourth-order errors using Chapman–Enskog and linear shear analysis.
evidence_signal: Taylor–Green and obstacle-flow stability maps show an enlarged stable domain; all three operators achieve second-order Taylor–Green convergence, with E-RLBM error about 6% above BGK and 40% below RLBM.
watch_item: Kinetic relaxation changes higher-order errors in a lattice-direction-dependent way, so improved stability does not guarantee improved accuracy.
